name: Cabergoline on cycle

card.summary: Use of the prescription dopamine agonist cabergoline alongside anabolic steroids such as nandrolone or trenbolone, which users say keeps prolactin-related side effects from interfering with training and physique goals.
card.note: Prescription drug used off-label; dopamine agonists carry their own side effects.

quick.overview:
Cabergoline is a prescription drug that lowers prolactin. In bodybuilding circles, people using 19-nor steroids such as nandrolone and trenbolone discuss it as a way to deal with sexual side effects they associate with raised prolactin, so that they can keep training and sustain muscle gain.

The practice is community-driven. Researchers have not tested cabergoline in steroid users, and forum users themselves disagree about whether the steroids raise prolactin directly.
quick.how: Users describe checking blood prolactin and taking cabergoline orally when they believe levels are high or when symptoms appear. Dosing and sourcing are not covered here.
quick.risks: Medically it is used for hyperprolactinaemia, Parkinson disease and related conditions. Reported side effects include nausea, dizziness, low blood pressure, insomnia and depression, and rare fibrotic reactions; some forum users mention dopamine-agonist withdrawal and mood effects.

lead: Cabergoline (caber) is an ergot-derived dopamine D2 agonist that suppresses prolactin release from the pituitary [1]. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums, it is discussed as an add-on during courses of nandrolone or trenbolone, where users blame elevated prolactin for libido and erectile problems that disrupt training and recovery.

Medically, cabergoline treats hyperprolactinaemia and prolactinomas, Parkinson disease and lactation suppression, and was patented in 1980 and approved for medical use in 1993 [1]. It is prescription-only in the United States and Australia [1]. Its use with anabolic steroids is off-label and is documented only in community discussion.

Forum posters describe caber as a short-term fix for high prolactin in men whose doctors suspected it was suppressing testosterone, and others warn about side effects and dopamine-agonist withdrawal [2].

chain: Steroid use raises user concerns about prolactin-related sexual side effects
Users stay on their training plan and keep muscle gain
angle.text: Users say controlling prolactin protects libido and function so they can continue a muscle-building course. This is a user-reported rationale rather than a tested outcome.

paras: Approved uses include hyperprolactinaemia and prolactinomas, with Parkinson disease treated in some regions; off-label uses include countering SSRI sexual side effects and reducing ovarian hyperstimulation risk in IVF [1].

Posters on T Nation discuss cabergoline mainly in the context of elevated prolactin on testosterone replacement, where urologists prescribed it for short periods, and mention side effects such as irritability and agitation after higher doses [2]. One poster warned about dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome and said that messing with dopamine is serious business [2].

Common effects are nausea, constipation, dry mouth, drowsiness, insomnia, dizziness, depression, low blood pressure and oedema; rare fibrotic reactions in lung and pericardium occur and cabergoline has been linked to valvular heart disease at higher doses [1].
No studies found in steroid users. Registered trials of cabergoline cover other uses, such as preventing ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome in IVF [3].

timeline.event: Cabergoline patented; developed by Farmitalia-Carlo Erba [1].

lore.intro: Discussed on T Nation threads on 19-nor steroid side effects and on prolactin management [2].

claims.claim: Caber is needed on nandrolone or trenbolone to prevent prolactin-driven sexual side effects.
claims.believers: Users attribute loss of libido and erectile difficulty on these compounds to prolactin and say lowering it helps [2].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested this in steroid users; the drug's labelled uses are other conditions [1].
